questions.q: Let $A \left(-1, 1\right), B  \left($3, 4\right)$~and $C  \left(2, 0\right)$ be given three points. A line $y = mx, m > 0$~, intersects lines $AC$ and $BC$~at point $P$ and $Q$ respectively. Let ${A}_{1}$ and ${A}_{2}$ be the areas of $\Delta ABC$ and $\Delta PQC$~respectively, such that ${A}_{1} = 3{A}_{2}$, then the value of $m$ is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$P ≡ \left({x}_{1},m{x}_{1}\right)$

~$Q ≡ \left({x}_{2},m{x}_{2}\right)$

${A}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left|$\begin{cases}3 & 4 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 1 \\ - 1 & 1 & 1\end{cases}$\right| = \dfrac{13}{2}$

${A}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left|$\begin{cases}{x}_{1}& m{x}_{1} & 1 \\ {x}_{2} & m{x}_{2} & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{cases}$\right|$

${A}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left|2\left(m{x}_{1} - m{x}_{2}\right)\right| = m\left|{x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right|$

${A}_{1} = 3{A}_{2} ⇒ \dfrac{13}{2} =$=3m\left|{x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right|$

$⇒ \left|{x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right| = $\dfrac{16}{6m}

$AC: x + 3y = 2$

$BC: y = 4x - 8$

$P: x + 3y = 2 & y = mx ⇒ {x}_{1} = $\dfrac{2}{1 + 3m}

$Q: y = 4x - 8 & y = mx ⇒ {x}_{2} = $\dfrac{8}{4 - m}

\left|{x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right| = \left|$\dfrac{2}{1 + 3m} - \dfrac{8}{4 - m}\right|

$= \left|$\dfrac{- 26m}{\left(1 + 3m\right)\left(4 - m\right)}\right| = \dfrac{26m}{\left(3m + 1\right)\left|m - 4\right|}

=\dfrac{26m}{\left(3m + 1\right) \left(4 - m\right)}$

\left|{x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right| = \dfrac{13}{6m}$

$\dfrac{26m}{\left(3m + 1\right) \left(4 - m\r$right)}=\dfrac{13}{6m}

$⇒ 12m^{2} = - \left(3m + 1\right)\left(m - 4\right)$

$⇒ 12m^{2} = - \left(3m^{2} - 11m - 4\right)$

$⇒ 15m^{2} - 11m - 4 = 0$

$⇒ 15m^{2} - 15m + 4m - 4 = 0$

$⇒ \left(15m + 4\right)\left($m - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ m = 1$

$

questions.q:
The point $P \left(a, b\right)$ undergoes the following three~transformations successively:
\left(a\right)$~reflection about the line $y = x .$
\left(b\right)$~translation through $2$~units along the positive~direction of $x -$~axis.
\left($c\right)$~rotation through angle $\dfrac{π}{4}$about the origin in~the anti-clockwise direction.

If the co-ordinates of the final position of the point~$P$ are \left(- $\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{7}{2}\right),$then the value of $2a + b$ is& equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Image of $A \left(a, b\right)$ along $y = x$ is $P^{'}\left(b, a\right) .$

Translating~it $2$ units along positive direction of~$x -$axis it becomes $P^{"}\left(b + 2, a\right) .$

Now, applying Rotation theorem

$- $\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{7}{2}$i = \left( \left($b + 2\right) + ai\right)\left($cos\dfrac{π}{4} +isin\dfrac{π}{4}\right)$

Multiplying the complex numbers we get,

$\dfrac{- 1}{2} + \dfrac{7}{2}i = $\left(\dfrac{b + 2}{2} - \dfrac{a}{2}) +$i\left(\dfrac{b + 2}{2} + \dfrac{a}{2})

$⇒ b - a + 2 = - 1 . . . \left(1\right)$

and~$b + 2 + a = 7 . . . \left(2\right)$

$⇒ a = 4; b = 1$

$⇒ 2a + b = 9$

$

questions.q: If the line $3x + 4y - 24 = 0$ intersects the $x$-axis~is at the point $A$ and the $y$-axis at the point $B,$~then the incentre of the triangle $OAB,$~where $O$is the origin, is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The& $x$~intercept of the line~$3x + 4y - 24 = 0$~can be obtained by putting~$y = 0$~i.e.~$3x - 24 = 0$

$⇒ x = 8$

Hence, the point~$A$~is~\left(8, 0\right) .$

Now, the~$y$ intercept of the line~$3x + 4y - 24 = 0$~can be obtained by putting~$x = 0$~i.e.~$4y - 24 = 0$

$⇒ y = 6$

Hence, the point~$B$~is~\left(0, 6\right) .$

In~$∆ OAB,$~we have~$OA = b = 8, OB = a = 6$~and~$AB = c = \sqrt{\left(8 - 0\right)2 + \left(0 - 6\right)2} = \sqrt{64 + 36} = 10$~units.

And, we know that the co-ordinates of incentre~$I$ of a triangle with vertices~\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right), \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)~and~\left({x}_{3}, {y}_{3}\right)~and having~length of the sides opposite to these vertices as~$a, b$~and~$c,$~respectively, ~is

$I ≡ \left(\dfrac{a{x}_{1} + b{x}_{2} + c{x}_{3}}{a + b + c}, \dfrac{a{y}_{1} + b{y}_{2} + c{y}_{3}}{a + b + c}\right)

$⇒ I ≡ \left(\dfrac{6\left(8\right) + 8 \left($0\right) + 10 \left(0\right)}{24}, \dfrac{6 \left($0\right) + $8\left($6\right) + $10\left($0\right)}{24}\right)

$⇒ I = \left(2, 2\right) .$

$⇒ p = 8$

Now~\left($AC\right)2 = \left($1 - 7\right)2 + \left(-$2 - 4\right)2 = 72 = 9p$

and~$AC^{2} + p^{2} = 72 + 64 = 136$

=\dfrac{1}{2} \left[18 + 18 \times $\dfrac{13}{5}\right]

Given coordinates of triangle& $ABC$,~$A ( a, 0 ) , B ( b, 2b + 1 ) , C ( 0, b )$

Area$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left|$\begin{cases}a & 0 & 1 \\ b & 2b + 1 & 1 \\ 0 & b & 1\end{cases}$\right|$

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left[a ( b + 1 ) + b^{2}\right] = \pm 1$

$ab + a + b^{2} = \pm 2$

If $2$~is positive~

$a = \dfrac{2 - b^{2}}{b + 1}$

If $2$is negative

$a = \dfrac{- 2 - b^{2}}{b + 1}$

Sum of possible values of $a = \dfrac{2 - b^{2}}{b + 1} + \dfrac{- 2 - b^{2}}{b + 1}$

$= \dfrac{- 2b^{2}}{b + 1}$

$⇒ 3k - b = \sin t - \cos t . . . \left(ii\right)$

Eliminating~$t$ from above two equation \left(i\right) \text{ and } \left($ii\right)$, we get

\left(h - $\dfrac{a}{3}\right)$2 + \left($k - $\dfrac{b}{3}\right)$2 = $\dfrac{2}{9}

So, \left(h, k\right)$ lies on the circle whose centre is $\left(\dfrac{a}{3}, \dfrac{b}{3}),now comparing with~\left(1, $\dfrac{1}{3}\right)~we get,$a = 3, b = 1$

Hence~$a^{2} - b^{2} = 8$

$

questions.q: A triangle has a vertex at $( 1, 2 )$ and the mid points of the two sides through it are $( - 1, 1 )$ and $( 2, 3 )$ . Then the centroid of this triangle is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let co-ordinates of $B = \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)
$∴ $\dfrac{{x}_{1} + 1}{2} = -$1 & $\dfrac{{y}_{1} + 2}{2} =$1$
$⇒ {x}_{1} = - 3, {y}_{1} = 0$
$∴ B = ( - 3, 0 )$
Let co-ordinates of $C = \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)$
$∴ \dfrac{{x}_{2} + 1}{2} = 2 \text{ and } \dfrac{{y}_{2} + 2}{2} = 3$
$∴ C = \left(3, 4\right)$
Let centroid $G = \left(h, k\right)$
$h = \dfrac{1 + {x}_{1} + {x}_{2}}{3} = \dfrac{1 - 3 + 3}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}$
$k = \dfrac{2 + {y}_{1} + {y}_{2}}{3} = \dfrac{2 + 0 + 4}{3} =2$
$∴$ Centroid, $G = \left(\dfrac{1}{3},2\right)

questions.q: Let $A$ be the set of all points  \left(\alpha, \beta\right)$ such that the area of triangle formed by the points  \left(5, 6\right),$~\left(3, 2\right)$ and  \left(\alpha, \beta\right)$ is $12$ square units. Then the least possible length of a line segment joining the origin to a point in $A,& is :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:Area of triangle formed by& \left(5, 6\right), \left(3, 2\right) \text{ and } \left(\alpha, \beta\right) = 12squareunits$

$∴ \dfrac{1}{2}\left|$\begin{cases}\alpha & \beta & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{cases}$\right| = 12$

$⇒ \left|$\begin{cases}\alpha & \beta & 1 \\ 5 & 6 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{cases}$\right| = 24$

$⇒ \alpha\left(6 - 2\right) - \beta\left(5 - 3\right) + 1\left(10 - 18\right) = \pm 24$

$⇒ 4\alpha - 2\beta - 8 = \pm 24$

$⇒ 4\alpha - 2\beta = 32, 4\alpha - 2\beta + 16 = 0$

$⇒ 2\alpha - \beta - 16 = 0, 2\alpha - \beta + 8 = 0$

So point will be either~ \left(\alpha, 2\alpha + 8\right), \left(\alpha,2\alpha -16\right)$

For the point~ \left(\alpha,2\alpha +8\right)$,

Distance from origin
$D = $\sqrt{{α}^{2} + ( 2\alpha + 8{)}^{2}} = \sqrt{5{α}^{2} + 32\alpha + 64} \left(∵ \beta =$=2\alpha +8\right)$

$⇒ D^{2} = 5{α}^{2} + 32\alpha +64$

For maximum or minimum length,

$\dfrac{d\left(D^{2}\right)}{d\alpha} ==$10\alpha +32 = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = - $\dfrac{16}{5}

$∴ \beta = $\dfrac{- 32}{5} +$8 = $\dfrac{8}{5}

$∴ D = $\sqrt{\left(- \dfrac{16}{5}\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{8}{5}\right)2} = \dfrac{8}{5}\sqrt{5} = \dfrac{8}{5}

Similarly if~$\beta =$=2\alpha -16, D = \sqrt{{α}^{2} + \left(2\alpha - 16\right)2} = \sqrt{5{α}^{2} - 64\alpha + 256}$

$∴ D^{2} = 5{α}^{2} - 64\alpha +256$

For maximum or minimum length,

$\dfrac{d\left(D^{2}\right)}{d\alpha} =0$

$⇒ 10\alpha -64 = 0$

$∴ \alpha = \dfrac{32}{5}$

$∴ D = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{32}{5}\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{64}{5} - 16\right)2} = \dfrac{16}{5}$at~$\alpha = \dfrac{32}{5}$
So, least possible length of line segment is~$\dfrac{8}{5}$

$
